UP did nothing to the gameplay object (the block is still at its original position). DOWN also did nothing. LEFT rotated the block 45° counterclockwise (into a diamond shape), and RIGHT rotated it back.
Hmm, wait. Maybe LEFT/RIGHT rotates the block around its own center, and the reason the diamond appeared to shift is due to the rendering of the rotated shape. The center of the diamond: rows 23–35, columns 20–28 → center (29, 24). The center of the rectangle is (28, 31.5). These are different, so it's not a pure rotation around the center.
Another possibility: LEFT moves the block left by one "step" while rotating it 45°. RIGHT moves it right and rotates it back. So the block is rolling! Like a square rolling to the left: rotate 45° around the bottom-left corner... hmm.
Actually, let me think about it this way: the block is rolling on the ground? But the block is floating above the white block.
Let me reconsider: maybe LEFT/RIGHT moves the block horizontally by a fixed distance, and the rotation is a visual "tilt" during movement that gets canceled out by the opposite direction. That seems weird.
Let me test: LEFT LEFT (two in a row) and see where the block ends up. And also test SPACE.
No wait. Maybe the game is this: the purple block is the "player" and it moves in the direction of the arrow keys, but it can only move when there's a path... UP and DOWN did nothing. LEFT moved it (with rotation), and RIGHT brought it back. Maybe the block only moves horizontally, and the rotation is part of the movement animation (the block tilts as it moves). But the final state after LEFT was a diamond shape, not a rectangle — that was the final state, not an animation.
Let me try pressing LEFT twice in a row and observe the state after each press.
